subject: Post-demo confirmation: where prompts & generated text are retained
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Tang <sarah.tang@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo confirmation: where prompts & generated text are retained

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups I promised on the call about how Redwood treats prompt text and model output (so your security/procurement team can review):

- Ask from your side: confirm what parts of the request/response lifecycle are persisted, where they live, and default retention windows. Also you asked whether any customer data may be used for model training or shared across accounts.

Immediate next steps:
1) I attached a short PDF with our PII handling summary (redwood-pii-data-handling.pdf).
2) Below I put the concise answers; happy to set a short sync with our Security team if you want official attestation.

Summary answers (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): by default we do not use customer prompts or outputs to train public models. For debugging/abuse-detection, request/response logs are retained by default for 30 days and are accessible via the Console.
- Logging: prompt + output logs can be disabled on your account (log retention = 0) or configured to a custom retention (e.g., 7/30/90 days) through the Console or API.
- Residency: data stored for logs is kept in the region tied to your account (we have US and EU regions). If you require EU-only residency, we can provision your account in eu-west-1.
- Private/Dedicated: Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) can be configured so logs never leave your environment; we support customer-managed KMS and HSM for encryption at rest.
- KV cache & runtime state: ephemeral, kept in-memory or on-host for the call, not persisted to long-term object storage.

Attachment: redwood-pii-data-handling.pdf (brief; includes SOC 2 and dataflow diagrams).

If you can confirm the security contact I should send the attestation to (or want the short security sync), I’ll schedule.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Tang <sarah.tang@medlytics.com>

Cc: privacy@medlytics.com
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 17:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo confirmation: where prompts & generated text are retained

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our privacy and engineering leads (privacy@medlytics.com copied):

1) When you say logs are "retained by default for 30 days" — is that configurable per-project or per-account? Can we set per-environment (prod vs. staging) policies?
2) For hosted accounts, are there any backups/snapshots that might include prompt/output text outside the 30-day window (e.g., object storage backups, disaster recovery snapshots)?
3) Can you confirm whether model providers or ops engineers at Redwood can access raw prompts/outputs? Is there RBAC/audit logging for access to historical requests?
4) For redaction: do you support automatic PII redaction at ingestion (names, emails, SSNs) or is that customer-side before sending prompts?
5) If we need EU-only residency and 0-day retention, what changes operationally and what SLA/contract language do we need?

Can you put answers inline so we can forward to procurement? Also attaching a short internal checklist we use — we’ll fill once we have your answers.

—Sarah
Sr. Product Manager, MedLytics

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Tang <sarah.tang@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo confirmation: where prompts & generated text are retained

Hi Sarah — answers inline below. I kept each one short so your team can paste into the checklist. Happy to expand or have Security join.

1) Configurability of retention:
- Per-account by default; we can scope per-project via separate subaccounts or separate API keys tied to different retention policies. For Dedicated/Private you get full control. We can set per-environment retention via Console by creating distinct workspaces (prod/staging) and applying retention at the workspace level.

2) Backups / snapshots:
- Hosted: we do not persist prompt/output text in long-term backup snapshots by default. Logs that are retained (the 30-day window) live in encrypted object storage in the account region and are included in our short-term day-based retention only. Disaster-recovery infrastructure is designed to restore service metadata and configuration; it does not contain customer payloads beyond the configured log retention window. If you require policy-level guarantees, we can add contractual language that excludes prompt/output from DR snapshots.

3) Access controls / audit:
- Access: Ops and support do not have unrestricted access to raw prompts/outputs. Access requires an audited troubleshooting workflow (ticket-based, RBAC) and is recorded in our audit logs.
- Audit logs: admin read events and support access requests are retained and exportable (CSV/JSON) for 365 days by default.

4) Redaction options:
- We offer two approaches:
  a) Customer-side: recommended — redact/filter before sending (best for PHI).
  b) Ingestion-time helper: optional SDK middleware that performs pattern-based redaction (emails, SSNs, credit-card-like numbers). This is configurable but not enabled by default. We can run an initial PII scan on a sample of requests during POC to estimate the reduction.

5) EU residency + 0-day retention:
- Operationally: we provision an EU-dedicated account region, disable host-side logging for your API key, and configure retention=0.
- Contract: we provide a data-residency addendum and a logging/retention appendix (we can include explicit 0-day retention clause). For on-prem/VPC we can sign a deployment addendum and support personnel access controls.

Other notes:
- Training: we do not use customer traffic to train our public models unless you opt in via a program-level agreement.
- Runtime caches: KV caches are ephemeral (per-session) and are not written to long-term storage.

Attachments: I re-attached the PDF and a link to the demo recording for your team to review.

If that looks okay, I can have our Security lead (Marissa) prepare a one-page attestation and a suggested contract clause for procurement. Would you like that on your letterhead or ours?

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
